_note: Written by the scheduled web & social sweep (and by hand). Every item needs a sourceUrl that was opened and checked. kinds: event (needs title+start+url, or just a Luma url), program (application windows), news (recaps, announcements), override (corrects a crawled event by id).

items.title: TreeHacks 2027
items.note: Stanford's flagship 36-hour hackathon. Open to enrolled undergrad and grad students worldwide; Stanford students are not auto-accepted.

items.name: Y Combinator — Winter 2027 batch
items.note: On-time deadline passed Nov 2 at 8pm PT; YC still considers late applications but cannot promise when it will reply. On-time applicants hear back by Dec 11. Batch runs January–March in San Francisco.

items.name: a16z speedrun
items.note: SR008 runs February 1 to April 16, 2027 in San Francisco. a16z says applications sent after November 1 are considered for the following residency; it reviews applications year-round. Up to $1M investment.

items.name: Berkeley SkyDeck — Batch 24
items.note: Applications for Batch 24 open in January. Batch 23 starts Nov 2, 2026.

items.name: TreeHacks 2027 hacker applications
items.note: Event Feb 12–14, 2027 at Stanford. Travel, meals and lodging covered for accepted hackers.

items.foundVia: Falcon Hacks site (via Hack Club Bay Area list)

items.name: South Park Commons Founder Fellowship — Spring 2027
items.note: Fall 2026 applications are closed. SPC says Spring 2027 applications open later this year; no date given.

items.name: Z Fellows
items.note: One-week program, mostly virtual, ending with an in-person day in San Francisco or New York. Applications reviewed on a rolling basis with no deadline. Optional $10,000 investment at a $1B cap.

items.name: PearX — W27
items.note: Regular applications for W27 closed Oct 4; applications submitted after that are reviewed on a rolling basis. Pear has offices in San Francisco and Menlo Park.

items.name: Entrepreneur First — San Francisco residencies
items.note: EF says it accepts applications for its U.S. funding and fellowships and San Francisco residencies on a rolling basis. Its Bridge Residency in SF (Winter 2027, 8 weeks for young Europeans) starts February 2027.

items.name: AI Grant — Batch 4
items.note: Applications for Batch 4 are closed; no date given for the next batch. $250k investment on an uncapped SAFE for pre-seed and seed AI companies. The Summit and Demo Day are in San Francisco.

items.title: Viam and MongoDB ran a Robot Hackathon on physical AI in San Francisco
items.body: Teams built physical AI applications on real robot arms using Viam for robot software and MongoDB Atlas for robot data, at the Robotics Center of Silicon Valley on Oct 29–30.

items.title: VapiCon 2026
items.venue: Festival Pavilion at Fort Mason, 2 Marina Blvd
items.note: Two-day voice AI conference for engineering and product leaders building voice agents. Ticketed; prices are not listed in the page text.

items.name: Founders, Inc. — funding and campus
items.note: Apply with what you are building for a chance at an invite to the Fort Mason campus in San Francisco and a first check. Founders, Inc. says it replies within a month; no deadline is given.

items.title: YC ran Haunted Hacks: Real-Time AI Edition in San Francisco
items.body: Y Combinator hosted a one-day Halloween hackathon on Oct 31 with tracks for stateful apps built on Terse Durable Actors and agent-to-agent communication with Agent Relay. The best overall project was promised a guaranteed YC interview.

items.foundVia: Luma search for San Francisco hackathons

items.title: Fireworks ran a Deploy Buildathon with Microsoft and NVIDIA in San Francisco
items.body: Teams of 2 to 5 deployed a model for a task of their choice, built an evaluation and tuned a tradeoff against a baseline in one day on Nov 2. Prizes were $10,000, $5,000 and $3,000 plus an NVIDIA DGX Spark; winners were not posted on the event page.

items.title: 2026 Epic AI MegaJam (in person)
items.note: Two-day game jam: teams of up to five build a playable game in Unreal Engine or UEFN. In-person attendance needs an Eventbrite ticket; submissions also need a separate itch.io jam registration. Epic says space is limited.
items.foundVia: Epic Developer Community forum post, Nov 1
Web search (Luma, VexoHacks at Y Combinator)

items.title: Own Your Intelligence
items.venue: Fisher Bay Observatory Gallery and Terrace, Exploratorium, Pier 15
items.note: Free evening event hosted by LangChain with Harrison Chase speaking; more speakers to be announced. Space is limited and registrations are approved by LangChain.
items.foundVia: Web search for Harrison Chase / LangChain events

items.title: Neo ran its second annual Neo Hackathon in San Francisco
items.body: An invite-only hackathon for Neo-invited teams of 2 to 4 on Nov 6–8, with 46 participants and judges from Anthropic and OpenAI. Winning projects are marked in the Devpost gallery, including a steerable weather balloon and a sword-fighting robot.

items.name: Conviction Embed — 7th cohort
items.note: Conviction says applications are open for the 7th cohort of Embed, its program for early AI-native founding teams, with rolling admissions. $250K investment on an uncapped MFN SAFE plus compute credits; includes an in-person retreat in San Francisco. No deadline given.

items.title: Cerebral Valley ran the AIE Code Summit 2026 Hackathon in San Francisco
items.body: A one-day, in-person hackathon with Meta, Google DeepMind, MongoDB, Subquadratic and Fetch.ai, with $11,000 in total prizes.

items.title: Silicon Valley Innovation Challenge 2026 — Finalists Showcase
items.note: SJSU student innovation competition; finalist teams present at the showcase. SJSU says 2026 registration is open through YouNoodle.

items.title: Conviction held Demo Day for the seventh Embed batch in San Francisco
items.body: About ten founders from Embed Batch 7 presented to investors at Conviction's demo day on Nov 12.

items.title: YC ran the Naïve Autonomous Company Hackathon in San Francisco
items.body: A two-day YC hackathon ending Nov 8 where teams built agent-run companies; first place got a guaranteed YC interview.

items.title: AI Hack for Freedom IV
items.organizer: AI Freedom Lab, with Human Rights Foundation and Presidio Bitcoin
items.note: Three-day hackathon where teams led by activist captains build tools for human rights work. Prize pool of $25k paid in BTC.

items.title: HBSA, SCET and Anthropic ran Hack with Claude in Berkeley
items.body: HBSA and UC Berkeley SCET hosted a Claude build session with Anthropic on November 13 in Berkeley.

items.title: Immerse the Bay 2026 XR hackathon wrapped at Stanford
items.body: The Nov 13–15 XR hackathon at Stanford listed $5,800+ in cash prizes plus hardware and credits from Visko and ManageXR. Winning projects are marked in the Devpost gallery, including Moonbase Managed, Cloudbound and Story Bricks.

items.name: StartX — Summer 2027 cohort
items.note: StartX says Summer 2027 applications open mid-December. For founders with a Stanford affiliation (students, alumni, faculty, staff).

items.title: The Big Hack Game held its Stanford vs Berkeley Demo Day in San Francisco
items.body: HarnessRouter and TokenRouter hosted judging for the Stanford vs Berkeley hackathon on November 20. The event page listed a $6,000 cash prize pool plus $6,000 in OpenAI credits across five awards.

items.title: Boat Hackathon held its Show Boat Demo Day aboard the Klamath in San Francisco
items.body: The first Boat Hackathon ended on November 21 with an invite-only demo day on the historic ship Klamath at Pier 9, co-hosted by The AI Collective.

items.title: Hackallax: Presented by Parallax & Anthropic
items.note: Two-day in-person hardware hackathon at the Parallax factory using its fabrication equipment. Challenges: build an air-powered motor or a freestyle build. Maximum team size is five; prizes include Bambu Lab H2S 3D printers and Claude API credits. Sponsored by Founders Fund, Lux Capital, Diffusion and Eclipse.
items.foundVia: Web search (Anthropic hackathon San Francisco December 2026)

items.title: X Square Robot ran an Embodied AI Hackathon in San Francisco
items.body: Solo builders and teams of up to three built on real robots on Nov 21–22, with an awards ceremony on Nov 22. Listed prizes were $5,000, $3,000 and $1,000, plus a $200 stipend for each qualified participant; winners were not posted on the event page.

items.title: Berkeley and Stanford student teams faced off at the Grok Bot Hackathon in San Francisco
items.body: A four-hour build session ahead of the 129th Big Game, with teams of two to four from the same school competing across tracks before onsite judges.

items.title: tokens& and AWS Builder Loft ran a Personal Agents Hackathon in San Francisco
items.body: A one-day hackathon on building personal agents that work outside chat apps, judged by engineers from Meta, Cursor, Intuit and Amplitude.

items.title: Pangram, Kino, Capy and Paper ran the SF Non-Slop Hackathon
items.body: A one-day, in-person hackathon on Nov 24 asking builders to use AI to make something intentional, with $1,000 cash prizes from each of the four sponsors. Registration required host approval.

items.title: Multiplayer AI Hackathon at AWS Builder Loft in San Francisco
items.body: A Thanksgiving-week hackathon on Nov 23 for building AI agents that act like characters, interacting with each other and with people in worlds the teams create.

items.title: Willow, Emergent and You.com ran Speech to Ship in San Francisco
items.body: A one-day hackathon at Emergent HQ on Nov 20 where builders drew a random city, business and customer, then built an app by voice. Winners shared $5K in credits plus hardware prizes.

items.title: Sundai, Autolab and Egbe ran the Recursive Self Improvement Hack: Autonomous Agent Businesses in San Francisco
items.body: A one-day hack on Nov 22 at RSI House on building tools that let projects run and improve themselves without a human in the loop. Registration required host approval.
items.org: Recursive Self Improvement · Sundai · Autolab · Egbe

items.title: IntelliPro Group held Founder Pitch Day #5 on robotics and physical AI at Stanford
items.body: Selected robotics and physical AI startups gave 7 to 10 minute pitches to investor judges, followed by live Q&A, on Nov 21. Founders applied to pitch.
